title: Persistence Basics
description: Learn to persist React Query cache to survive page reloads and browser sessions.

data.text: Cache persistence stores the React Query cache in a durable storage medium so that data survives page reloads, browser restarts, and even temporary offline periods. Without persistence, every refresh clears the cache and forces a loading state.
Persistence is especially valuable for mobile users on unreliable networks. Showing cached data instantly while validating in the background feels much faster than a blank loading screen.
data.title: Mobile UX

items: localStorage: Synchronous, 5-10MB limit, works in all browsers.
IndexedDB: Asynchronous, large capacity, better for big datasets.
sessionStorage: Cleared when tab closes, useful for temporary caching.
data.title: Options
Basic localStorage persistence

items: User-specific data that rarely changes: profile, settings, preferences.
Reference data: countries, categories, static lookups.
Offline-first applications: PWAs, mobile web apps.
data.title: Good Candidates

data.text: Do not persist sensitive data like auth tokens or personal information in localStorage. It is accessible to any script and persists across sessions.
data.title: Security
Persistence Basics Key Points
points: Persistence stores cache beyond page reloads.
Persist only non-sensitive, relatively static data.
Combine with background refetching for freshness.
data.takeaway: Persistence is the foundation of offline-capable React Query applications.
